'''Vermilic''' was a [[Hutt/Legends|Hutt]] [[Kajidic/Legends|kajidic]] and one of the younger clans among the other Hutt kajidics. Unlike more traditional Hutt families, Vermilic’s operations centered on the production and distribution of exotic [[Foodstuff/Legends|foodstuffs]] and intoxicants considered unusual within [[Hutt Space/Legends|Hutt society]]. The kajidic became particularly well known for farming the popular Hutt delicacy known as the [[Carnovian eel]]. During the early years of the [[New Republic/Legends|New Republic]], a young member of the Vermilic clan triggered a major trading collapse that lasted for three [[Standard month/Legends|months]]. As a result of this economic disaster, the Vermilic kajidic was eventually forced into bankruptcy.

==History==
Only a few thousand [[Standard year/Legends|years]] old, Vermilic was among the younger [[Hutt/Legends|Hutt]] [[Kajidic/Legends|clans]] by the time of the [[Declaration of the New Order|proclamation]] of the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]]. Consequently, it was not included in the [[Clans of the Ancients|Clans of the Ancients]] and did not possess its own [[Throneworld/Legends|throneworld]] within [[Bootana Hutta/Legends|Bootana Hutta]]. It regularly pushed the limits of Hutt law and tradition, which caused conflicts with the Clans of the Ancients. In fact, some of the younger Vermilic held Hutt commerce laws in such disdain that they neither knew nor understood them well. As such, they operated far from the traditional seats of Hutt power and pursued unconventional enterprises and schemes. At the same time, they were also involved in the production and distribution of soft [[Spice/Legends|spice]].<ref name="LH" />

[[File:Carnovia-TEA.jpg|left|thumb|280px|The planet Carnovia served as the base for Vermilic's operations.”]]
Vermilic's base of operations was also unusual. [[Carnovia]] was known for [[Carnovian eel|eel]] farming, as well as the production of exotic [[Foodstuff/Legends|foodstuffs]] and intoxicants – activities that were quite typical for the Hutts. The eels from Carnovia were popular Hutt snacks, and the labor-intensive [[Farm/Legends|farming]] required many [[Slavery/Legends|slaves]]. As such, the Vermilic operation relied on a tried-and-true Hutt tradition: slave labor.<ref name="LH" />

However, instead of employing equally traditional food preparation methods, Vermilic used its long-cultivated knowledge of foodstuffs to produce cheap imitations of in-demand processed foods, which its members distributed outside of [[Hutt Space/Legends|Hutt Space]], particularly to [[Abregado-rae/Legends|Abregado-Rae]], [[Toydaria/Legends|Toydaria]], [[Syvris/Legends|Syvris]], and [[Daalang/Legends|Daalang]]. [[Minalod]] the Hutt, the leader of the clan, entrapped and kidnapped [[Scientist/Legends|scientists]] from Hutt slave [[Species/Legends|species]] to provide the expertise needed to create these imitations. The most skilled among them worked and lived in the underwater dungeons of Minalod's [[Floating Palace|Floating Palace]], which sat at the center of a great lake, surrounded by shallow- and deep-water Carnovian eel pens.<ref name="LH" />

Around [[6 ABY/Legends|6 ABY]],<ref name="TERC">''[[The Essential Reader's Companion]]''</ref> a young Vermilic Hutt disintegrated one of his clan [[Hutt counselor|counselors]], violating one of the [[Hutt Commercial Laws]]. As a result, trafficking with other Hutt clans ceased for three [[Standard month/Legends|months]] and the Vermilic clan was bankrupted.<ref name="HS">{{StoryCite|story=Hutt and Seek|book=Tales from the New Republic}}</ref>

One of the Hutts of this clan, [[Dribba Vermilic Scaiti]], was interested in linguistics and wrote the book ''[[Huttese Ain't What It Used To Be]]'', in which he examined the influence of the [[Galactic Basic Standard/Legends|Galactic Basic Standard]] on the [[Huttese/Legends|Huttese]] language.<ref name="TWW">{{Hyperspace|url=hyperspace/source/writtenword/index.html?page=1|text=The Written Word|int=The Written Word}}</ref>

==Behind the scenes==
The Vermilic clan was first mentioned in the short story ''[[Hutt and Seek]]'', which was included in the anthology ''[[Tales from the New Republic]]'', published in [[1999]].<ref name="HS" /> More information about this kajidic was later presented in the regional supplement ''[[Lords of Nal Hutta]]'' for [[Fantasy Flight Games]]' ''[[Star Wars: Edge of the Empire]]'' [[roleplaying game]] series, released in [[2015]].<ref name="LH" />
